report.summary: An incident involving checkout timeouts on UPI payments occurred on 2026-10-04, with symptoms beginning at 13:41 UTC. The investigation concluded that an external third-party latency spike in the partner-bank-api caused upstream worker pool exhaustion in upi-gateway, which subsequently triggered timeouts and error rate spikes in payments-api and mobile-bff.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Partner Bank API Latency Spike Causing Worker Exhaustion

supporting.note: Shows partner-bank-api latency spike beginning at 13:41 UTC, which precedes all other dependent service anomalies.
Shows upi-gateway latency anomaly starting at 13:43 UTC, directly following the partner bank latency increase.
Confirms upi-gateway workers were exhausted because they were waiting on partner-bank-api.
Shows payments-api timing out when calling upi-gateway.
Shows payments-api latency p99 anomaly starting at 13:45 UTC.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Fraud Service Configuration Change Induced Processing Delays

supporting.note: Configuration change on fraud-service occurred shortly before the incident onset.

contradicting.note: Latency started rising at 13:41 UTC, whereas logs specifically show workers waiting on partner-bank-api rather than fraud-service.
Worker pool exhaustion is explicitly attributed to waiting on partner-bank-api, not fraud-service.

facts.text: upi-gateway latency p99 anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:43:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 10665.76ms.
upi-gateway error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:46:00+00:00, peaking at 13.72%.
payments-api latency p99 anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:45:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 10772.92ms.
payments-api error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:47:00+00:00, peaking at 12.58%.
payments-api CPU usage anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:46:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 57.2%.
payments-api logged repeated timeout errors calling upi-gateway POST /v2/collect after 10000ms.
mobile-bff error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:47:00+00:00, peaking at 4.67%.
upi-gateway logged worker pool exhaustion rejecting requests due to being busy waiting on partner-bank-api.
partner-bank-api latency p99 anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:41:00+00:00, peaking at 9237.07ms.
fraud-service configuration was modified at 2026-10-04T13:30:00+00:00 to raise velocity threshold from 5 to 7 transactions/min.

assumptions: The underlying cause of the partner-bank-api latency is an external issue at the partner bank.

timeline.event: fraud-service rules changed to raise velocity threshold from 5 to 7 transactions/min
partner-bank-api latency_p99 anomaly begins, reaching baseline to 8349.7 ms
payments-api latency_p99 anomaly begins and partner-bank-api error rate anomaly begins
payments-api CPU usage anomaly begins and upi-gateway error rate anomaly begins
payments-api error rate and mobile-bff error rate anomalies begin, alongside upi-gateway worker pool exhaustion logs

recommended_actions.action: Coordinate with the external partner bank provider to investigate the root cause of the latency spike on partner-bank-api.
recommended_actions.rationale: The incident root cause stems directly from performance degradation at partner-bank-api beginning at 13:41 UTC.

recommended_actions.action: Implement circuit breakers or aggressive timeout fallbacks between upi-gateway and partner-bank-api to prevent thread and worker pool exhaustion.
recommended_actions.rationale: Worker pool exhaustion at upi-gateway caused widespread downstream cascading timeout failures in payments-api.

recommended_actions.action: Review alerting thresholds for upstream external dependencies to detect third-party latency anomalies before worker pools are fully exhausted.
recommended_actions.rationale: Early detection of external dependency issues can prevent cascading checkout failures for end users.
